Short DescriptionSPREAD builds Engineering Intelligence for complex products. Our AI-native platform gives automotive OEMs, defense primes and industrial manufacturers one connected view of their product data, and Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Bosch and Rheinmetall already run it. We are backed by HV Capital, DTCP, La Famiglia and Salesforce, won the SPARK AI Innovation Award, and made LinkedIn's Top Startups in DACH list.Role: Getting a first meeting with an engineering director at an OEM is the hardest step in our funnel, and this role owns it. You sit between Business Development and Revenue Operations, report to our Head of Revenue, and work every day with the BDRs and Account Executives. Half your time goes to pipeline, which means finding the right accounts and people and building the plays that reach them; the other half goes to the engine behind those plays, which you build with Claude Code rather than by hand, so the sales team spends its hours in conversations instead of research and data entry. Your work counts when it turns into meetings and pipeline, not when another dashboard ships. The person we picture did BDR or SDR work, liked the tooling and the process more than the cold calls, and now builds agents because they want to.Your Mission• Design, launch, and test outbound plays into automotive and industrial engineering accounts, each with a hypothesis and a conversion number, track each play from first touch to qualified opportunity, and retire the ones that do not convert.• Run cadences across email, phone and LinkedIn in German and English together with the BDRs and AEs, and write first touches good enough that the reps reuse them.• Turn our Account News feed, which scores news, hiring and leadership changes every night, into meetings with the people those signals point to.• Build account maps, contact scores and segments for campaigns and events, so every play starts from the right twenty people rather than the right two thousand.• Run Clay enrichment triggered from Salesforce, so reps get emails, phone numbers and titles without asking anyone.• Build the AI agents the sales team uses every week (meeting prep, account research, post-call Salesforce updates, outreach drafts) and win adoption through short demos, an agent of the week, and fixing whatever made people stop using one.• Extend our GTM dashboard, a Next.js app on Vercel that reads Salesforce, with the funnel, BDR activity and account penetration views Business Development needs.• Keep the funnel data in Salesforce clean, from leads and contacts to campaigns, activity capture, and attribution, so the numbers in every pipeline review hold up.• Run the content engine for sales, from the Brand Hub to the tooling that turns Product Marketing's material into decks, films and one-pagers a rep can send the same dayWhat success looks like in the first 12 months• After 3 months, two outbound plays are live end to end with reported conversion, Clay enrichment and the BD funnel view are yours, and you write our first touches yourself.• After 6 months, the BDRs run a play library without you, the whole sales team uses one of your agents every week, and qualified pipeline traces back to your plays.• After 12 months, you are the person everyone asks "how do we get into this account?", and the top-of-funnel engine runs every week without a push.Your Experience Must-have• 2 to 4 years in B2B go-to-market as a BDR, SDR, growth or sales ops hire at a startup or scale-up.• Meetings you booked yourself, so you know what a good first call feels like from the rep's side.• Automations in Clay, n8n, Zapier or Make that other people relied onSomething you shipped with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or a similar AI coding tool, and daily work with Claude or ChatGPT.• Salesforce at a working level, meaning reports, fields, list views and basic flows.• A habit of running experiments (hypothesis, small test, numbers, next step) and a preference for launching something rough on Tuesday over polishing it for a month.• Fluent German and English, since most of our outreach goes to German engineering leaders.Strong plus• SQL or SOQL, Python or TypeScript.• Salesforce admin experience, or time in Salesloft, Apollo, or HubSpot.• Experience selling to automotive, manufacturing, or engineering-software buyers.• A side project, newsletter, or LinkedIn presence that shows you can create demandWhy SPREAD?You sell AI for engineering to the biggest names in automotive and industry, with a product that customers run in production. Our reps already work with Claude agents, and you build the next ones, so what you ship on Monday is in front of the sales team by Wednesday. You have a direct line to the founders and the sales leaders, and your plays get discussed rather than filed. We pay competitively and add an annual learning budget, workation options, a Deutschlandticket mobility budget and Urban Sports Club. You get 30 vacation days plus one paid volunteering day a year, and lunch at the Berlin office three times a week.How we hire: A 30-minute call, a 3-hour work sample you do on your own time, two or three interviews, and references. From first call to offer usually takes less than a month.ContactDmytro İefymenkorecruiting@spread.aiSPREAD AIKöpenicker Str. 40c | 10179 BerlinStay connected—follow us on LinkedIn for the latest insights and updatesAbout usSPREAD is pioneering Agentic Engineering Intelligence . Our low-code platform transforms fragmented hardware and software product data into dynamic Product Twins , creating an AI-ready knowledge base that powers smarter decisions and automation across the entire product lifecycle.At the heart of our technology lies the world’s first Universal Engineering Information Model (EIN) — a semantic framework that connects domain-specific and lifecycle data into a federated Engineering Intelligence Graph , continuously evolving over time. The SOS Children's Villages worldwide Hermann-Gmeiner-Fonds Deutschland e.V. is an independent, non-denominational children's rights organization. With its headquarters in Munich and offices in Berlin and Düsseldorf, the organization has been supporting the global projects of SOS Children's Villages since 1963. 200 employees are committed to the vision of "For a world that lets you grow". With almost 3,000 programs in over 130 countries, the organization offers help to children, young people and families in need through education, medical care and family strengthening. The focus is on strengthening the family, sustainability, children's rights and cultural sensitivity.   International Operations manages the funding of our international partner's projects. We work with internal and external bodies to ensure that donations are used appropriately and provide reporting. For this department we are looking for a Finance Manager for Project Funding (f/m/d) for our Munich or Berlin office. This is a full-time position (38,5 hours per week) available immediately. The position has a fixed term to cover parental leave. Your tasks Working alongside our programme departments, you will review funding applications from our international partners, focusing on project budgets. You will prepare funding agreements and submit them to our Board for approval. This ensures that donations are used to support effective projects in areas such as child and youth care and family strengthening.  You will also be responsible for arranging the transfer of funds. During project implementation by our partners, you will check their budgets, reports and audits. This will ensure that our funds are used for their intended purpose and support project change management.  You will work closely with colleagues from our programme departments and act as the main point of contact for several of our international partners on financial matters.  As part of a major overhaul of our grant-making processes, you will introduce and develop new procedures with our partners. To this end, you will be involved in internal change projects.  You will assist with internal monitoring and reporting, including quarterly forecasts and annual budgeting.  You will also support our fundraising efforts and annual audit by providing analysis and financial information. Your profile A degree in Business Studies or equivalent with a solid professional grounding in numbers and financial processes. Experience in financial controlling and accounting, as well as in the not-for-profit sector, would be advantageous but is not required. Your excellent English skills enable you to understand complex subjects and express yourself confidently. The ability to speak and write French is advantageous. You also have a good command of German. Experience of working in the field of international development cooperation in West Asia or West Africa would be an advantage. You are eager to learn, and you are interested in understanding complex structures. You can work independently and enjoy working in a team. You can recognise when each type of work is required. You know how to navigate difficult situations and find mutually beneficial solutions. You have excellent Microsoft Office skills, particularly in Excel.   Knowledge of digital project management and accounting systems such as SAP would be an advantage. What we offer A diverse, inspiring, and responsible role in a professionally managed, internationally active non-profit organization·       Opportunities for professional development and the chance to be part of an international network An open ear for new ideas and impulses, and the opportunity to help shape our work, processes and digital systems Work-life balance through flexible working hours, compensatory time off, and the option to work remotely (including from abroad) Numerous benefits like employer funded pension and financial allowance for childcare Meal allowance, subsidy for the Deutschlandticket, subsidized EGYM Wellpass Interesting further training opportunities SOS Children's Villages adhere to strict child safeguarding principles and maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse. Therefore, during recruitment, we not only consider personal and professional suitability, but also the willingness to act according to our child protection guidelines and values. We require an extended police clearance certificate upon employment. Diversity is important to us. At SOS Children's Villages Worldwide, we actively stand against racism and discrimination, and we welcome applications from people regardless of their ethnic, national, or social background, gender, disability, age, or sexual orientation. If you are excited about this challenging role, we look forward to receiving your application soon! SOS-Kinderdörfer weltweit  Ridlerstr. 55 80339 München

jobs.occupation: PhD Positions in Agentic AI for Medical Image Analysis (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.The Division of Medical Image Computing (MIC) at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, starting in January 2027, is offering PhD Positions in Agentic AI for Medical Image Analysis.The Division of Medical Image Computing (MIC) is recruiting PhD candidates to develop AI agents that interpret medical images, use analysis tools, evaluate intermediate results, and adapt their approach based on evidence and feedback.Candidates will join a collaborative research environment with clinical partners, extensive computing infrastructure, and connections to initiatives such as Helmholtz Imaging.Your TasksWe investigate how AI agents can combine medical images with clinical information, plan and execute analytical steps, learn from feedback, assess intermediate results, and respond appropriately to uncertainty or failure. Approaches may include reinforcement learning, multimodal learning, vision-language models, planning, tool-augmented language models, probabilistic modelling, and classical medical image analysis.Candidates may work primarily in one of several application areas:1. multimodal agents for prostate cancer diagnosis and treatment support;2. auditable analysis of longitudinal imaging for tumour-response assessment;3. federated multimodal agents connecting oral imaging with systemic health information; or4. or reinforcement learning for agents that navigate and integrate complex data across medical and other scientific domains.The individual PhD topic will be developed jointly based on the candidate’s interests, expertise, and the methodological questions arising across these applications.You will:- develop agents that combine medical images with clinical text and other information;- investigate reinforcement learning for planning, tool use, feedback integration, and iterative improvement;- apply agentic methods to segmentation, annotation, quantitative analysis, or scientific data exploration;- establish rigorous evaluation methods covering accuracy, robustness, generalisation, uncertainty calibration, failure detection, and appropriate abstention; and- collaborate with methodological and clinical researchers, publish your results, and contribute reusable software or benchmarks.Your ProfileYou should have:- A master’s degree in computer science, data science, mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline- A strong foundation in machine learning and strong Python programming skills- Practical experience with a deep-learning framework such as PyTorch- Experience in at least one relevant area, such as reinforcement learning, computer vision, language models, multimodal learning, or medical-image analysis- An analytical and collaborative working style and good communication skills in EnglishPrevious experience with medical data is helpful but not required. We also welcome candidates with strong machine-learning fundamentals who want to develop expertise in agentic AI.What you can excpect:- Scientific freedom to develop your own methodological research question- Close supervision and exchange within a cohort of PhD researchers- Access to extensive GPU infrastructure, medical-imaging resources, and established research software- Collaboration with international machine-learning and clinical partners- Support for conference participation, open-source contributions, and professional development- Fully funded PhD submissionPlease submit:- your CV- academic transcripts- a brief research statement of no more than one page describing a question in agentic AI that interests you- your preferred application area, or a ranking of the available areas- your master’s thesis or another representative piece of scientific work- links to relevant publications, software, or code repositories, if available- Instead of a generic motivation letter, please use your research statement to explain which scientific question you would like to investigate, why it matters, and how you might approach itWe Offer- Excellent framework conditions: state-of-the-art equipment and opportunities for international networking at the highest level- Access to international research networks- Doctoral salary with the usual social benefits- 30 days of vacation per year- Flexible working hours- Possibility of part-time work- Family-friendly working environment- Sustainable travel to work: subsidized Germany job ticket- Unleash your full potential: targeted training and mentoring through the DKFZ International PhD Program and DKFZ Career Service- Our Corporate Health Management Program offers a holistic approach to your well-beingAre you interested?Then become part of the DKFZ and join us in contributing to a life without cancer!Contact:Constantin Ulrich HarsyPhone: +49 (0) 6221/42-3552Duration: The positions are initially limited to 3 years.Application Deadline: December 2, 2026Applications by e-mail cannot be accepted.Please also note that we cannot return applications submitted by post.We are convinced that an innovative research and working environment thrives on the diversity of its employees. Therefore, we welcome applications from talented people, regardless of gender, cultural background, nationality, ethnicity, sexual identity, physical ability, religion and age. People with severe disabilities are given preference if they have the same aptitude.Notice: We are subject to the regulations of the Infection Protection Act (IfSG). Therefore, all our employees must provide proof of immunity against measles.

jobs.occupation: Power Systems and Controls Engineer (f/m/d) (Ingenieur/in - Energietechnik)
jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day Join our dynamic team and immerse yourself in the exciting world of power systems and controls! You will build transient models for grid-connected converters and plants, including renewable energy systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS), HVDC, FACTS, and microgrids. Imagine defining and developing controller concepts that enhance the performance of converter-based assets, from inner controls to plant-level energy management. You will investigate the interactions among various systems, ensuring robust performance during normal operations and faults. Your expertise will drive innovation as you apply data analytics and AI/ML methods for predictive maintenance and load forecasting, all while mentoring the next generation of engineers in this critical field.How You’ll Make an Impact * Develop and validate transient models for converter-based grid assets, including renewables, BESS, HVDC, FACTS, industrial loads, data centers, and microgrids* Design, tune, and assess control strategies from converter inner controls to plant-level energy management and supervisory functions* Implement grid-following and grid-forming controls, including synchronization, voltage/frequency support, and fault ride-through capabilities* Analyze interactions between converter controls, plant controllers, and protection systems to optimize system performance and reliability* Perform dynamic, transient, and small-signal studies to evaluate system behavior and support controller tuning in weak and low-inertia grids* Apply advanced analytics and AI/ML techniques for forecasting, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, while providing technical leadership and mentoringWhat You Bring* Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Power Systems, Control Engineering, or a related field with a focus on power systems and controls* Extensive professional experience in power-system modeling and studies, including development and validation of RMS and EMT models* Strong understanding of power-system dynamics, stability, fault response, and control interactions* Practical expertise in converter-based technologies and control architectures, including grid-following and grid-forming controls* Proficiency with industry-standard simulation tools (e.g., PowerFactory, PSCAD/EMTDC, MATLAB/Simulink) and programming in Python, MATLAB, or similar environments* Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience in data analytics/AI/ML considered an advantage; fluent English required, German a plusAbout the TeamIn our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability.
